title: British Skiing’s New Dynasty: The Carrick‑Smith Brothers Take the Slopes by Storm
excerpt: Three brothers sweep a New Zealand podium, backed by Olympian mum and ski‑coach dad, aiming for World Cup glory.
body:
## A Historic Podium Sweep
At a slalom race in New Zealand last September, the Carrick‑Smith brothers—Luca, Freddy and Zak—made history by claiming all three medals. It’s the first time three siblings have achieved a clean‑sweep in FIS alpine skiing, and the trio celebrated with the Union Jack proudly displayed on their bibs. Freddy, 19, described the moment as “super special” and said the goal now is to replicate it on the World Cup circuit or even at the Olympics.

## Family‑Run Coaching and Funding
The brothers are a true family affair. Their mother, Emma Carrick‑Anderson, is a four‑time Winter Olympian for Team GB, while their father, Phil Smith, runs Snoworks ski courses across Europe. With their parents as coaches, the boys say they get a level of understanding and support that a “random coach” could never provide. The twins, Freddy and Zak, grew up racing together, with older brother Luca pushing them forward.

Funding their dream is a massive challenge. The family needs roughly £320,000 each season, relying on a mix of GB Snowsport’s Alpine Foundation support, sponsorships and crowdfunding. Training costs can be steep— a two‑and‑a‑half‑hour session in Colorado runs about $1,200 (£914)—and the parents juggle three separate programmes as the brothers compete in Finland, Austria and elsewhere.

## Looking Ahead: From Alpine Cup to Olympic Dreams
Freddy already sits on Great Britain’s World Cup squad, while twin Zak and Luca compete on the Europa Cup circuit. The brothers hope their recent success will catapult them onto the world stage, following in the footsteps of British skiing families like the Bells and the Baxters. Emma, who now coaches full‑time after leaving her own job, stresses the importance of treating her sons as “humans first, athletes second,” a mindset she believes will help them weather the inevitable ups and downs of elite sport.

The Carrick‑Smith family’s story is still being written, but their podium sweep in New Zealand has already signaled the rise of a potential new dynasty in British skiing.

sources.title: Are these three brothers British skiing's next family dynasty?
